decision: Spans are a waterfall, indented by depth, colored by service with a legend, and the slow span outlined
why: Latency is about where time goes on the critical path; a waterfall shows it without reading numbers.
value: The 612 ms connection wait jumps out immediately.

decision: Span attributes follow OpenTelemetry semantic conventions plus our own (db.pool.wait_ms, deploy.id, idempotency.key, Kafka offset)
why: Standard names make any tool understand the data; the custom ones carry the facts this business debugs by.
value: A trace answers which version, which pod, which deploy and which message.

decision: Logs carry the trace id, so the trace shows exactly its log lines
why: Searching logs by time window during an incident drowns you in other requests.
value: Context in one place, from span to log line.

decision: An AI note explains why the trace is slow, citing the span, the deploy and pool metrics, and links to the open problem
why: Reading a waterfall is a skill; the note makes the conclusion explicit and checkable.
value: Anyone on the team can act on a trace, not just the expert.

decision: Every consequential action in the portfolio ends with a 'View trace' link that lands here
why: The trace is the thread tying Counter, Pay, Circle, Mesh and Product Hub together.
value: Reviewers follow one click from a button to the system behind it.
